response: {"turns":[{"id":"M1:T121","text":"On performance, error-mode recovery really depends on the subsystem, and each one's Functional specification defines it. Normally with a fatal error there's no recovery except shutting down and restarting that subsystem. But if an instrument fails, we might keep going by rescheduling to observations that don't need that particular instrument. For serious errors we may be able to continue with degraded performance, so for example if automatic tracking fails we'd go to manual tracking, and other errors might mean running with a different instrument. Under normal conditions the number of warnings should be small, and the system should monitor the rate of warning messages, because if it goes up that might mean some tuning or maintenance is appropriate. Ideally the subsystems catch those conditions before they reach the OCS level. And failures shouldn't cascade, so one subsystem failing shouldn't affect the other working subsystems, communication links included."},{"id":"M1:T122","text":"Let's move to the operating system. What do we need to know there?"},{"id":"M1:T123","text":"So there'll probably be software below the IOC level, but it shouldn't need downloading, except maybe for upgrades. Typically it sits in ROM or FLASH memory. While it's connected to the system, any access to that embedded software goes strictly through software in the IOC, so from outside the IOC it just looks like part of the electronics. It's not considered part of the Gemini software, but for maintenance it's obviously an advantage if it conforms to the Gemini software requirements."},{"id":"M1:T124","text":"What about external software packages?"},{"id":"M1:T125","text":"For archiving, all astronomical data get saved into the Archiving system. Storage and transport of astronomical data will be in FITS format, and on-line access to the archiver goes through STARCAT."},{"id":"M1:T126","text":"Okay, and hardware requirements?"},{"id":"M1:T127","text":"For development hardware, workstations have to match the specified software standards and give a well-designed development environment, including cross-support for VxWorks development if needed. They're expected to be state-of-the-art, CPU and communications support, in a scaleable family, so development systems can migrate as technology advances. We assume they support Ethernet IEEE-802.3 and FDDI interfaces for communications. Internal data formats have to be compatible across the development workstations, and SCSI-interface peripherals need to be available. And when we pick the final target systems, we'll consider reliability, manufacturer support and upgrade capability of the development systems."},{"id":"M1:T128","text":"Got it."},{"id":"M1:T129","text":"And on communication hardware?"},{"id":"M1:T130","text":"The backbone LAN can't be Ethernet, because of the bandwidth requirements.
